title: Regional GPU Upgrade & Availability Plan Q3 2025
content:
Sheet title: Regional GPU Upgrade & Availability Plan Q3 2025

Overview:
This sheet captures planned maintenance windows for rolling NVIDIA driver + runtime upgrades across our regional GPU pools, expected capacity drain percentages, fallback/traffic routing, pre/post validation, and rollback criteria. Primary goal: complete driver rollouts (current baseline driver 535.x -> target 537.29) with <5% sustained throughput loss for production-hosted customers and no SLA misses for Dedicated pools.

Summary timeline:
- Week 1 (canary): us-east1 small canary (5% of capacity) — 2025-07-07 02:00-08:00 UTC
- Week 2 (region pilot): us-west1 (20% of capacity) — 2025-07-14 02:00-12:00 UTC
- Week 3 (scale): eu-west1, eu-central1 staggered (2-day windows) — 2025-07-21 to 2025-07-24
- Week 4 (APAC): asia-southeast1, asia-northeast1 — 2025-07-28 to 2025-07-30
- Week 5 (catch-up / rollouts for Dedicated customers): 2025-08-04 to 2025-08-08

Key assumptions and targets:
- Target driver upgrade: NVIDIA driver 537.29 + CUDA 12.1 compatible runtime.
- Affected instance types: A100-40GB (a100-40), H100-80GB (h100-80) pools only in this cycle.
- Minimum reserve buffer: keep 12% of each region's GPU capacity untouched for emergency traffic rehoming.
- Maximum controlled drain per maintenance wave: 30% of regional capacity (default 20% for production, 5% for canary).
- SLO guardrails: <3% 95th-pct tail latency increase for hosted API; Dedicated customers must be consulted before any >15% drain.

Pre-maintenance checklist (runbook steps):
- Confirm smoke-test suite and golden prompts for evaluation (owner: eng-evals).
- Reserve emergency rehome capacity: tag 12% GPUs as "emergency-reserve" and validate autoscaler excludes them.
- Notify impacted Dedicated customers 7 days prior with exact windows and drain percents.
- Validate image/driver artifacts in staging infra: driver package checksum, installer script acceptance tests.
- Run one full workload on canary pool (latency, memory, kv-cache correctness, quantization regression quick checks).
- Ensure on-call SRE & serving-runtime lead are present during window.

Execution play (per wave):
1) Pre-window (T-4h): run health sweep, confirm metrics ingestion, increase replica headroom by 10% where possible.
2) Drain step (T-3h to T-2h): mark selected machines cordoned, shift new allocations away; drain active sessions by preferring prefix cache reuse when possible.
3) Upgrade step (T-2h to T+2h): apply driver, restart GPU daemon, run smoke tests. Keep simultaneous upgrades per AZ <= 50% of that wave's targeted drain to avoid correlated failures.
4) Validation (T+2h to T+4h): run golden prompt suite, perf microbenchmarks (latency p50/p95/p99), and load sample traffic at 50% normal rate.
5) Uncordon / capacity restore: reintroduce machines gradually, monitor error rates for 30m.

Traffic shaping and routing plan:
- Use smart routing policy: if region's available capacity < required threshold for a route, route to fallback region with <40ms added latency SLA where feasible.
- For latency-sensitive customers, enable region-affinity thresholds to avoid routing unless >30% of regional capacity is drained.
- Implement temporary token-based rate limits for new sessions in impacted regions if p95 latency increases >2x baseline.

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback triggers):
- Serving runtime OOMs across >3% of active containers post-upgrade during validation.
- Error rate increase >1% absolute on 5xx for an entire region for 15 continuous minutes.
- Unrecoverable GPU driver kernel panic or nodes fail to come back to Ready state after 20 minutes.
- Quantization/precision regression detected on gold prompt failure rate >2% absolute.
If any trigger fires, mark wave failed, rollback to previous driver image from S3 backup, and schedule incident review.

Post-maintenance validation & metrics to capture (first 72 hours):
- p50/p95/p99 latency vs baseline (hourly)
- Tokens/sec per-GPU and tokens/sec per-cluster (compare to prior 7-day median)
- OOM and kernel panic events (count and stack traces)
- Customer error rates by product tier (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Cost-per-token delta (capture for Optimize team)

Open risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Driver incompatibility with older quantization path. Mitigation: keep quantization-compatible fallback images and test set that covers int8 paths.
- Risk: Autoscaler thrash under rapid drain. Mitigation: increase cooldown to 5m and preseed extra control-plane replicas.
- Risk: Regional capacity shortfall for scheduled Dedicated tenants. Mitigation: manual approval gate and postpone wave until alternate capacity confirmed.

Contact list and escalation matrix (primary -> secondary -> pager):
- Serving runtime lead: Maya Chen -> Tom Brooks -> SRE pager (oncall)
- Infra ops: Arjun Patel -> Priya Nair -> Infra pager
- Evals & QA: Samuel Ortiz -> Lena Fischer -> QA pager

Notes for postmortem if anything breaks:
- Capture the exact set of instance IDs and driver package SHA used.
- Preserve logs (journalctl, dmesg, GPU driver logs) and upload to incident bucket.
- Annotate metrics dashboards with downtime windows and correlate with traffic shifts.

Quick capacity calculation examples (for Wave 2, us-west1):
- Total GPUs: 240; planned drain 20% -> 48 GPUs offline
- Normal throughput baseline: 240 GPUs * 1.0 tokens/sec/GPU = 240 t/s
- Expected throughput after drain: (240-48) * 1.0 = 192 t/s (20% reduction).
- With emergency reserve 12% (29 GPUs), usable pool for rehome = 240 - 48 - 29 = 163 GPUs; this is worst-case rehome capacity before cross-region routing.

Appendix: quick smoke test commands and expected outputs (for SRE/ops):
- nvidia-smi -q -> returns driver version 537.29 and no GPU ECC errors
- container smoke: run ./perf-smoke.sh --model llama-2-13b --seq 512 -> p95 < 650ms on h100 test node
- golden prompt check: run ./golden-check --job canary-2025-07-07 -> pass ratio >= 98%

Document history: initial draft 2025-06-10 by Arjun Patel; staging updates and stakeholder review through 2025-06-18.

End of sheet.
